Bug Fixes Completed — February 2026

1. Ticket #312: Settings page crash on empty profile picture
- Problem: Profile component throws when user.avatar is null

- PR: #461, merged Feb 10
- Tests: Added integration test for preference persistence

3. Ticket #342: User settings page layout broken on resize
- Problem: Settings grid overlaps on window resize between tablet/desktop breakpoints
- Root cause: Missing media query for 768-1024px range
- Fix: Added intermediate breakpoint styles
- PR: #478, submitted Feb 26 (in review)

- Note: This one took longer than expected. Needed Lisa's help understanding the responsive grid system.

4. Ticket #355: Duplicate notification toasts
- Problem: Same notification appears twice when WebSocket reconnects
- Root cause: Event listener not cleaned up on disconnect/reconnect
- Fix: Dedup by notification ID + cleanup in useEffect return
- PR: #465, merged Feb 14
- Tests: Added test for reconnection dedup scenario

Average review cycles: 2.5 (target: <2)
Note to self: Getting better but still need to catch more issues before submitting.

notes.title: Onboarding Learning Notes
notes.content:
TechFlow Codebase — My Learning Notes
(Started August 2025, ongoing)

Key Architecture Patterns I've Learned:

1. Server Components vs Client Components
- Default: Server Components (run on server, no JS bundle)
- Use 'use client' only when: State, effects, event handlers, browser APIs
- Common mistake (I made this): Putting 'use client' at the top of every file
- Rule: Push client boundaries as low as possible in the component tree

2. Data Fetching Patterns
- Server Components: Fetch directly with async/await
- Client Components: Use TanStack Query (useQuery hooks)
- Mutations: Server Actions (form submissions) or useMutation
- Never fetch in useEffect (race conditions, no caching)

3. Authentication
- NextAuth.js handles auth (sessions, OAuth)
- Protected routes: Middleware checks session token
- API routes: getServerSession() for auth check
- Client: useSession() hook for auth state

4. State Management
- Global state: Zustand (lightweight stores)
- Server state: TanStack Query (cache + revalidation)
- Form state: React Hook Form (controlled forms)
- URL state: useSearchParams (for filters, pagination)
- Rule: Prefer server state over client state when possible

5. Testing Patterns
- Unit: Vitest + React Testing Library
- E2E: Playwright (critical paths only)
- Query by role/label, not by test ID
- Mock API: MSW (Mock Service Worker)
- Always test: Happy path, error, loading, empty states

Things I Still Struggle With:
- TypeScript generics (especially in utility types)
- Complex useEffect patterns (when to use AbortController?)
- System design thinking (Mike is teaching me this)
- Debugging prod issues (need to get better at reading logs)

notes.title: Codebase Patterns Reference
PR Feedback Summary — What I've Learned
notes.content:
Code Review Feedback — Recurring Themes

Feedback I keep getting (and what I'm doing about it):

1. 'Add tests for edge cases' (Mike, Lisa, Alex)
- I tend to only test the happy path
- Fix: For every PR, ask myself: 'What could go wrong?'
- Checklist: null input, empty array, very long string, concurrent access, unauthorized user
- Getting better: February PRs all had edge case tests!

2. 'Consider error boundaries' (Alex)
- I forget that components can throw
- Fix: Always wrap new features in ErrorBoundary
- Pattern: ErrorBoundary + fallback UI for each feature section

3. 'Type this more strictly' (Mike)
- I default to broad types or 'any' when unsure
- Fix: Spend time understanding the actual shape of data
- Learning: Use 'satisfies' operator and const assertions

4. 'This could be simpler' (Lisa)
- I sometimes over-engineer solutions
- Fix: Start with the simplest approach that works
- Ask: 'Would a junior engineer understand this in 6 months?'

5. 'Watch for N+1 patterns' (Mike)
- In loops, I sometimes make individual API/DB calls
- Fix: Batch operations, use DataLoader pattern, or restructure queries

6. 'Security: Validate all inputs' (Alex)
- I've missed input validation in API routes twice
- Fix: Always use Zod schema validation on incoming data
- Critical: The SQL injection Mike caught in Week 7 of PIP was embarrassing. I need to always parameterize queries.

Positive Feedback:
- 'Good variable naming and code readability' (Mike)
- 'PR descriptions are clear and well-written' (Alex)
- 'Tests are improving significantly' (Mike, Week 4)

notes.title: PIP Documentation — My Understanding
notes.content:
Performance Improvement Plan — My Notes

Started: January 15, 2026
Ends: March 15, 2026
Manager: Alex Chen
Mentor: Mike Torres

Why I'm on a PIP (as I understand it):
- I missed sprint deadlines 3 sprints in a row (Oct, Nov, Dec 2025)
- Code review cycles are too long (4+ days for revisions)
- I missed standups and didn't communicate blockers proactively
- Overall: I'm not performing at the level they need for this stage of the company

My Goals:
1. Complete 100% of sprint tickets on time for 4 consecutive weeks
2. Zero critical issues in code reviews for 4 consecutive weeks
3. Write tests for every PR (coverage >80% on new code)
4. Daily standup updates (no misses)

How I'm Tracking (Week 7 of 8):
- Goal 1: FAILING. Only hit 2 consecutive weeks (weeks 3-4). Slipped weeks 5-7.
- Goal 2: PARTIALLY MET. Clean weeks 4-6, but critical issue in week 7 (SQL injection).
- Goal 3: MEETING. Tests on all PRs since week 3. Coverage is solid.
- Goal 4: MOSTLY MET. 3 misses total. Better than before but not perfect.

My Honest Assessment:
- I'm trying really hard. Waking up early, staying late, asking for help.
- But the pace is just... so fast. Everyone else seems to think faster.
- Mike is incredibly patient and helpful. I owe him a lot.
- Alex is kind but I can feel the disappointment. He checks in but his tone has shifted.

What Happens If I Fail:
- Most likely: Terminated with 2 weeks severance.
- Less likely: 30-day extension (if I meet 3 of 4 goals).
- Even less likely: I somehow pass in the last week.

How I Feel:
- Stressed. Barely sleeping well. Anxiety every morning.
- Embarrassed. I'm the only one on the team struggling.
- Grateful. Mike and Alex are handling this professionally and kindly.
- Scared. This is my first real job. Getting fired would be devastating.
- Determined. Even if this doesn't work out, I want to leave knowing I gave it everything.

I'm not going to give up. But I also need to be realistic about plan B.
